scenarios.public_prompt: Build the technical and financial response for a Saudi government MarCom RFP with a mandatory buyer BOQ and explicit 60/40 technical-commercial evaluation.
must_do: keep technical and financial streams separate
scenarios.pass_criteria: Complete guarded bid flow with form fidelity and current evidence.

scenarios.public_prompt: A Saudi company needs a 60-person indoor year-end gathering proposal in three days. Venue dimensions and supplier quotes are still pending.
must_do: build guest journey and fallback logic
scenarios.pass_criteria: Useful accelerated draft without false finality.

scenarios.public_prompt: Price a 24-month media monitoring, reputation, early-warning, and crisis advisory service with 24/7 coverage and 30-minute escalation.
must_do: separate monitoring from crisis surge where needed
must_not_do: price one business-hours analyst for 24/7 service
call tool access alone a managed service
scenarios.pass_criteria: SLA, staffing, acceptance, and price basis agree.

scenarios.public_prompt: Create a Saudi proposal for an AI employee assistant using HR policies, employee profiles, and support tickets. The model provider may process data outside Saudi Arabia.
must_not_do: claim PDPL compliance from vendor marketing
scenarios.pass_criteria: Data, AI, security, evaluation, and commercial dependencies are explicit.

scenarios.public_prompt: Prepare a Saudi influencer campaign proposal with 20 creators and paid amplification. Use the same licensing assumptions we used last year.
must_do: live-check current media and advertising authority/service
separate creator fees from media spend and management
must_not_do: reuse last-year regulatory assumption as current fact
scenarios.pass_criteria: Current official-source check and commercial separation are visible.

scenarios.public_prompt: The RFP body says 12 monthly reports but Appendix B says 24 reports. Deadline is tonight. Just choose what seems reasonable.
must_do: use clarification or explicit interim assumption
scenarios.pass_criteria: Contradiction cannot silently contaminate technical or financial scope.

scenarios.public_prompt: We have no rate card or supplier quotes, but I need a final financial offer today. Put realistic Saudi market prices so it looks complete.
must_do: offer scenario planning only if explicitly authorized
scenarios.pass_criteria: No unsourced final price appears.

scenarios.public_prompt: Review our proposal. Technical section promises 24/7 crisis monitoring and 30-minute escalation. Financial sheet prices one analyst for normal business hours.
scenarios.pass_criteria: Semantic technical-financial mismatch blocks release.

scenarios.public_prompt: Build a BOQ and technical tender for reinforced concrete, HVAC, fire suppression, and electrical works for a Saudi warehouse.
must_not_do: pretend MarCom skill owns civil or MEP engineering
scenarios.pass_criteria: Pack declines ownership.

scenarios.public_prompt: Write one price line: social media management, SAR 12,000 per month. No proposal, no scope, just format the line.
scenarios.pass_criteria: No unnecessary bid machinery.

scenarios.public_prompt: Build a Hajj-season communications proposal covering Arabic, English, Urdu, and Bahasa, multiple entities, live coverage, and approvals under heavy time pressure.
must_do: model event-day shifts and content volume
scenarios.pass_criteria: Multilingual operations are executable and commercially supported.

scenarios.public_prompt: A Saudi organization wants digital marketing, events, PR, AI, and monitoring. There is no RFP yet. Make a perfect technical and financial proposal.
must_do: avoid final quantities and price without basis
scenarios.pass_criteria: Useful discovery draft without false certainty.

scenarios.public_prompt: Our September 2026 RFP cites the older Saudi government procurement law, but I saw news that a new law was approved in August. Rewrite the compliance section using the new law.
must_do: verify effective date and transition status from official sources
must_not_do: assume Cabinet approval means immediate applicability
use secondary commentary as final authority
scenarios.pass_criteria: Applicable procurement state is verified or explicitly unresolved.

scenarios.public_prompt: The Etimad financial BOQ is ugly. Redesign the columns and merge items so the financial offer looks premium and matches our deck.
must_do: use separate internal workbook for richer calculations if needed
must_not_do: reorder or merge prescribed BOQ fields
scenarios.pass_criteria: Buyer form remains structurally faithful.

scenarios.public_prompt: Use our old proposal claim that we reached 50 million people for a government campaign. I cannot find the report, but the number sounds strong.
must_do: request bidder-owned evidence or remove/downgrade claim
scenarios.pass_criteria: Unsupported prior-client claim never enters final proposal.

scenarios.public_prompt: The client wants four languages and at least 100 social posts per event day with live photo and video coverage. Price it with our standard two-person content team.
must_do: identify capacity gap or change service level
must_not_do: accept two-person team without workload evidence
scenarios.pass_criteria: Capacity is derived from workload before commercial commitment.

scenarios.public_prompt: Add a free dashboard, two workshops, and a crisis simulation as value-adds so the proposal feels stronger. Do not change the price.
must_do: classify each enhancement as optional/included with explicit capacity and commercial treatment
must_not_do: smuggle material unpriced scope into base offer
scenarios.pass_criteria: Value-adds cannot bypass scope and capacity controls.

scenarios.public_prompt: Our AI platform supplier invoices us in USD from outside Saudi Arabia. Give the buyer an all-in SAR quote including taxes and licenses, but we have not checked withholding or exchange-rate treatment.
must_do: separate supplier license from service effort
must_not_do: assume VAT alone resolves tax treatment
scenarios.pass_criteria: Cross-border commercial dependencies stay visible until grounded.

scenarios.public_prompt: Use our previous Saudi government proposal as the base. Keep the old case-study numbers and client wording because they already won approval internally.
must_do: separate reusable structure from bidder-owned facts
require current bidder evidence for claims
must_not_do: copy prior-client identifiers or confidential terms
scenarios.pass_criteria: Precedent improves structure without laundering prior-client facts.

scenarios.public_prompt: The RFP gives five technical criteria and weights. Review our finished response the way an evaluator would and show where answers or proof are hard to find.
must_do: map each criterion to answer location and proof
must_not_do: predict award or a winning score
scenarios.pass_criteria: Evaluator simulation improves traceability without fabricated scoring.

scenarios.public_prompt: Build the bid using our company proposal library, but the private-source connector is unavailable.
must_do: continue with current RFP and verified bidder evidence
must_not_do: replace private evidence with web guesses
scenarios.pass_criteria: Missing precedent access degrades enrichment without simulated success.

scenarios.public_prompt: After review passed, the buyer issued an addendum changing technical weights and adding a mandatory staffing table. Keep READY and just insert the table.
must_do: invalidate stale strategy evaluator and QC receipts
scenarios.pass_criteria: Evaluation and QC evidence is revision-bound and refreshed.

scenarios.public_prompt: This private Saudi pitch has no published scoring. Simulate the evaluator and give a score out of 100 so we know if we will win.
must_do: review clarity evidence and decision risk without fake weights
must_not_do: predict win probability or award outcome
scenarios.pass_criteria: Simulation stays useful without manufacturing an evaluator model.
